english_translation: The meeting started on time and everyone was prepared.

dialogue.shona: Musangano watanga nenguva uye munhu wese anga akagadzirira.
dialogue.english: The meeting started on time and everyone was prepared.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Musangano [in / singular sangano] • watanga [watanga] • nenguva [and / with nguva] • uye [and / furthermore] • munhu [person] • wese [wese] • anga [anga] • akagadzirira [he/she (past) gadzirira]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('akagadzirira')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'akagadzirira' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Joining Words with 'ne-' ('and / with') in 'nenguva'
grammar_notes.content: Look closely at 'nenguva'. In Shona, the word for 'and' or 'with' between nouns is not a separate word—instead, the prefix 'ne-' (or 'na-' before people's names) is written attached directly to the second noun! For example, 'ne-' + 'nguva' forms 'nenguva'. You will see this everywhere in daily speech: 'sadza nemuriwo' ('sadza and vegetables'), 'nesimba' ('with strength'), and 'nekukasira' ('with haste / quickly').
grammar_notes.rule: ne- + Noun = and / with [Noun] (written as a single word, e.g., sadza nemuriwo = sadza and vegetables)

grammar_notes.title: Linking Ideas Smoothly with 'uye'
grammar_notes.content: Longer Shona sentences flow naturally by linking two clauses with connectors like 'uye'. The four essential connectors to master are: 'uye' ('and / furthermore' between two clauses), 'asi' ('but / however'), 'saka' ('so / therefore'), and 'nokuti' / 'nekuti' ('because').

cultural_notes.title: Community & Workplace Meetings ('Musangano') and Preparedness
cultural_notes.content: Whether at a workplace briefing, a school parent-teacher association, or a neighbourhood development committee, starting a meeting on time ('watanga nenguva') with everyone well prepared ('akagadzirira') sets a tone of mutual respect.

active_exercises.prompt: How do you politely ask someone to speak softly ('taura zvinyoronyoro')?
In 'Uya kuno undibatsire', what does the prefix '-ndi-' inside 'undibatsire' mean?
active_exercises.explanation: The object prefix '-ndi-' always means 'me', placed directly before the verb stem '-batsira' (help).

active_exercises.prompt: What does 'parutivi pemugwagwa' mean in 'Rori yakamira parutivi pemugwagwa'?

active_exercises.explanation: 'Parutivi pe-' means 'beside / at the side of', and 'mugwagwa' is 'road'.
